title: Seventy Cubits
logline: The morning after the earthquake of 226 BC, an old man walks up to the fallen Colossus and remembers the siege that orphaned him, the twelve years he spent building the god, and the day he first touched its face.
style: cinematic film still, Hellenistic Greek city of Rhodes in the 3rd century BC, historically accurate, natural light, 35mm, warm muted palette, no text, no modern objects, no medieval buildings

scenes.title: The fall, 226 BC
scenes.text:
They say the god fell in the night. The ground shook, the walls came down along the harbour, and in the morning my granddaughter came running to tell me that Helios was lying in the grass.

I am eighty-nine years old. I went down to see him anyway.

He broke at the knees. That is where we joined him, you see. I know. I was there.

shots.still: wide dawn view of a colossal fallen bronze statue lying broken in long dry grass on a hill above an ancient Greek harbour city, the huge legs snapped at the knees, rough stone rubble spilling from the hollow broken limbs, dust hanging in the air, collapsed stretches of city wall below
shots.motion: slow aerial drift over the fallen statue as dust settles in the morning light

shots.motion: the old man walks slowly away from camera up the path

scenes.title: The siege, 305 BC
scenes.text:
I was ten years old when Demetrius came. Two hundred warships, and behind them nearly a thousand little boats of traders, following like gulls behind a fishing fleet, waiting to pick over whatever was left of us.

My father rowed. Every man rowed, or carried stones, or stood on the wall. The slaves were promised their freedom if they fought, and they fought.

Then Demetrius built the City-Taker: a tower nine storeys high, clad in iron, pushed by more men than lived on our whole street.

shots.still: a vast ancient fleet of oared war galleys and small merchant boats filling the sea outside a walled Greek harbour city, hazy morning, seen from the city wall
shots.motion: the fleet rows slowly toward the city, oars rising and falling

shots.still: @boy stands on a stone city wall between Greek citizen soldiers in bronze helmets holding spears, staring out to sea
shots.motion: wind tugs at the boy's tunic, the soldiers shift their spears

shots.motion: the oarsmen pull in rhythm

shots.motion: the men strain and haul the blocks forward

shots.still: a colossal nine-storey wooden siege tower clad in iron plates on huge solid wheels, rows of shuttered firing ports, being pushed across a dusty plain toward a stone city wall by hundreds of men
shots.motion: the tower creeps forward, dust rising from its wheels

scenes.title: The night of fire
scenes.text:
One night the whole city threw fire at it. I carried pitch in a bucket until my arms stopped working. By morning the iron plates had fallen away like fish scales, and the tower crawled back out of range.

My father did not come home from the harbour that night.

A year after it began, Demetrius made peace and sailed away. He left his engines on the plain.

shots.still: night, hundreds of fire arrows and flaming missiles arcing from a city wall toward a giant iron-clad wooden siege tower, sparks and smoke
shots.motion: flaming missiles streak across the night sky and strike the tower

shots.still: @boy carries a heavy wooden bucket of pitch along a torch-lit rampart at night, face smeared with soot
shots.motion: the boy hurries along the rampart, torches flickering

shots.still: close shot at night of iron plates falling away from a burning timber siege tower, glowing timbers and embers
shots.motion: iron plates peel off and fall, flames spread along the timber

shots.still: grey dawn over a quiet ancient harbour, smoke drifting over the water, a single empty wooden rowing boat drifting
shots.motion: the empty boat drifts slowly through the smoke

shots.still: an abandoned giant scorched siege tower and catapults standing on a plain outside a Greek city wall in morning light, a fleet sailing away on the horizon
shots.motion: slow push toward the abandoned engines as the fleet recedes

scenes.title: The city's promise
scenes.text:
Rhodes buried my father at public cost. The city fed my mother, and paid my sister's dowry, and when I turned eighteen they called me into the theatre at the festival of Dionysus and gave me a suit of armour, in front of everyone, because I was the son of a man who had died for them.

I did not want to fight. I wanted to make something.

shots.still: a public funeral procession in an ancient Greek city, citizens carrying shrouded biers, women mourning in dark cloaks, a small boy walking beside a mother
shots.motion: the procession moves slowly past

shots.still: an ancient open-air Greek theatre packed with citizens at a spring festival, ivy garlands, a herald standing on the stage
shots.motion: the crowd stirs and murmurs, garlands move in the wind

shots.motion: the official places the helmet in his hands

shots.still: @youth alone at dusk holding a bronze helmet, looking down at it thoughtfully
shots.motion: slow push-in as he turns the helmet in his hands

scenes.title: The foundry
scenes.text:
They sold Demetrius's engines for three hundred talents, and with the money the people vowed a statue to the Sun. Chares of Lindos would make it: seventy cubits of bronze, taller than anything any of us had ever seen.

I went to the casting pits the first week. I was nobody. I carried charcoal.

Beside me worked Mys, a Carian, who could not vote, and a slave called Doros, who could not leave. We were paid the same: a drachma a day, and the same burns.

shots.motion: smoke billows as workers move between the furnaces

shots.motion: he turns the wax model slowly in the lamplight

shots.still: @youth carries a heavy basket of charcoal on his shoulder through the foundry smoke
shots.motion: he walks through the smoke toward camera

shots.still: three soot-covered workers pumping leather bellows at a glowing furnace: @youth, a Carian man with a red headband, and a slave with a cropped head
shots.motion: they pump the bellows and the fire flares

shots.still: molten bronze pouring from a clay crucible into a huge clay mould shaped like a giant bare foot, sparks flying
shots.motion: glowing bronze flows into the mould, sparks fly

scenes.title: The mound
scenes.text:
We cast him in rings, from the feet up. When one ring cooled, we heaped earth around it and built the next one on top, so the work was always on the ground, and the ground kept rising.

For twelve years I climbed a hill that we were making. Every year it was higher. Every year I could see a little further out to sea.

shots.still: a huge man-made earthen mound on a hill above an ancient Greek city, the tops of two colossal bronze legs rising from its summit, workers carrying baskets of earth up wooden ramps
shots.motion: slow crane up the side of the mound

shots.motion: he climbs steadily up the ramp

shots.motion: shadows lengthen as the workers move on the slopes

shots.still: @youth sits on the top of the earth mound at dusk eating bread and olives, looking out over the city to the sea
shots.motion: wind moves his hair, sails move on the distant sea

scenes.title: Philis
scenes.text: In the eighth year I married Philis, a shipwright's daughter, who laughed at the soot in my beard. The city had paid my sister's dowry. I paid Philis's father myself, out of bronze-worker's wages, and I was prouder of that than of the armour.

shots.still: a young Greek woman with dark braided hair in a plain madder-red dress laughing in a shipyard among half-built wooden ship hulls
shots.motion: she laughs and turns toward camera

shots.still: @youth and a young dark-haired woman at a simple Greek wedding feast in a courtyard at night, garlands, torches, family
shots.motion: torches flicker, the guests clap

shots.still: close shot: @youth counts silver coins stamped with a rose into an older man's open palm
shots.motion: the coins drop one by one into the palm

scenes.title: The face
scenes.text:
The last summer, we cast his head. I was on top of the mound when the mould was broken open, and there he was: a face as tall as a house, crowned with rays, looking out over the sea toward Egypt, where our grain came from.

I put my hand on his cheek. It was still warm.

shots.motion: chunks of clay fall away to reveal the bronze face

shots.still: @youth stands on the top of an earth mound beside the colossal bronze face of @helios, the man tiny beside it

shots.still: close shot: a man's soot-stained hand pressed against a giant smooth bronze cheek, heat shimmer in the air
shots.motion: the hand presses gently against the bronze

shots.motion: slow pan across the city toward the open sea

scenes.title: The festival of the Sun
scenes.text:
Then we took the hill away, basket by basket, and he came up out of the earth like a man standing up from a bath.

At the festival of the Sun we raced, and sang, and drove a chariot and four horses into the sea for him. My son sat on my shoulders and asked if the god could see us.

I said yes. I said: I made his left foot.

shots.still: hundreds of workers carrying away an earth mound in baskets, uncovering a colossal standing bronze statue of the sun god @helios with a crown of rays, draped in a bronze cloak, dust in the air
shots.motion: workers stream away down the slopes, dust drifts

shots.motion: slow push toward the statue, sunlight flaring off the bronze

scenes.title: The thumb
scenes.text:
Now he lies in the grass with his knees broken, and the kings of the world are sending us gifts. Ptolemy of Egypt offers three thousand talents to raise him up again.

But the oracle said no. Leave him where he lies.

I think the oracle is right. Let the ships come in, and the strangers walk up from the harbour and stand beside him, and try to put their arms around his thumb.

They won't manage it. I tried, this morning.

shots.motion: wind moves the grass, the old man sits very still

shots.motion: the ship glides into the harbour
